column4: Pixel-art game sprite in the style of 1990s Build-engine games (Duke Nukem 3D, Blood, Redneck Rampage): chunky visible pixels, a limited muted palette, strong simple shading, seen straight from the front at eye height, as one flat cut-out layer of things standing side by side on one floor line along the bottom edge, warm lamp light on them. Background must be flat solid pure magenta #FF00FF everywhere else, also between and above the things; no walls, no floor, no ceiling drawn, no shadow, no text, no border, no watermark. The furniture of a small wooden 1980s Czech holiday cabin room: on the left a single wooden bed with a red checked blanket and a white pillow, in the middle a small wooden table with a glowing table lamp and a mug on it and a wooden chair beside it, on the right a narrow wardrobe with a coat hanging on its door.

The inside of an old 1970s camping caravan: on the left a fold-down dinette table with a checked cloth between two benches with orange cushions, a kettle and two cups on the table, on the right a small cupboard with a gas stove on top and a hanging lamp glow.

Pixel-art sprite in exactly the same style as the reference image (a hand-painted 320x240 VGA close-up of a cork noticeboard from an early 1990s DOS adventure game): the same chunky dithered pixels, the same 256-colour palette, the same warm low light and the same straight-on view. A single object only, centred, filling most of the canvas, nothing else from the reference scene. Background must be flat solid pure magenta #FF00FF everywhere around the object, no cast shadow, no text, no border, no watermark. The object: one sheet of squared paper torn out of a school exercise book, a ragged torn edge along its left side, faint pale blue grid squares all over it, slightly creased and yellowed, a small white pushpin at the top middle, nothing written or drawn on it.
